chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us from his book, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Aamir narrated to us, from Abdul Malik ibn Atba, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever dies without knowing his Imam, dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).

key_terms.مِيتَةً جَاهِلِيَّةً: A death of ignorance (pre-Islamic era state of disbelief/ignorance)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of dying without knowing the Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores that recognition (*ma'rifa*) of the Imam is the cornerstone of faith, equating its absence with the spiritual blindness of pre-Islamic *Jahiliyyah*. Scholars emphasize that this 'recognition' extends beyond mere knowledge to include acceptance of the Imam's authority, making it a prerequisite for the validity of one's religious standing at the time of death.
